title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan

epigraph.quote: Refusing a mediocre risk-reward setup in a great industrial franchise is not pessimism; it is how capital survives to catch the next true inflection.
epigraph.author: Institutional Capital Allocation

web_blocks.html: We now combine Pass 1's quality audit (COMPOUNDER_PASS, PASS_WITH_WATCH) [27][28], Chapter 7's $355.00 Base Case [13], and Chapter 8's Stage 4 tape ($341.50; CAP_REJECTED) [14]. Dropping all bias toward our prior WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT call leads to a clean downgrade. General Dynamics owns scarce submarine and Gulfstream assets, yet four blockers—TREND, VALUATION, CASH_FLOW, and BUSINESS—remove our margin of safety. The earned verdict is REJECTED (TIER_0). Because GD is NOT_HELD (0 shares, 0 options), zero shares are sold and marginal cash stays 100% in reserve.

web_blocks.html: Holding Audit & Portfolio Context: GD is NOT_HELD in the consolidated US Schwab and Robinhood ledger (0 shares, 0 options). Zero shares need trimming or selling. Total US cash sits at just $2,540.35 (3.38% of $75,110.60 net worth) against a 22.0% Downtrend cash floor (38.8% > 50-DMA, 10 distribution days). Keeping 100% of marginal cash in Cash or T-Bills protects liquidity rather than chasing Stage 4 risk. We benchmark that choice against Stage 2 shortlist leader MCK ($1,069.72; 0.64:1 R:R from its $1,066.70 snapshot band top vs. $857.69 stop to $1,200.00, rising to 1.69:1 only in its $940.00–$985.00 shortlist entry zone) and outside Stage 2 peer LMT ($565.50; 16.98x Fwd P/E, 21.31% ROIC, 2.64:1 R:R to $645.00). Both receive 0% allocation until portfolio cash rebuilds toward 22.0%.

Four-Point Re-Underwriting Watchlist: Four concrete steps must happen before reopening a buy review. First, check Q4 2026 Note J filings (late January 2027) for closure of the SEC, DOJ, and DoW OIG Electric Boat subpoenas [27]. Second, confirm Congress passes full FY2027 appropriations past December 11, 2026 to fund Navy shipbuilding plans and convert $108.5 billion of unfunded backlog [22][27]. Third, track collection of the $1.2 billion Combat Systems unbilled receivable and verify Marine margins exceed 8.2% ex-EACs [27]. Also monitor GDIT execution under Amy Johnson against its $14.52 billion goodwill base [26][27][30]. Fourth, require Danny Deep's 2027 capital plan plus a confirmed Stage 1 base and Stage 2 reclaim above $358.35 [14][29].

Decision Trigger — What Changes REJECTED: Reopen an active buy review only if Note J Electric Boat subpoenas close without material clawback. Price must also either reset to $295.00–$310.00 or reclaim $358.35 on >=1.2x volume with Base Case R:R above 1.50:1. A break below $315.00 confirms the Bear Case path toward $245.00.

book_paragraphs: Every chapter of research now converges on one clean, unbiased decision. In Pass 1, General Dynamics retained its COMPOUNDER_PASS business quality because its nuclear submarine shipyards and Gulfstream large-cabin jets remain scarce strategic franchises. Yet when we re-tested the numbers and opened the live November 20, 2026 market tape, our prior WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT posture failed to survive scrutiny.

First, give the bulls their strongest honest case. Nine-month free cash flow surged 60.5 percent year over year to $4,827 million, Gulfstream posted a 1.4-times book-to-bill ratio with 14.5 percent operating margins and 119 deliveries, net funded debt dropped to $2,628 million after $1 billion of debt repayments, and total backlog sits at a record $220.3 billion. On the surface, 15.97 times trailing free cash flow looks cheap for a Tier-1 prime.

Now place the bear case beside it with equal rigor. In Note J of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q, GD disclosed August 2026 subpoenas from the SEC, DOJ Civil Division, and DoW Office of Inspector General investigating Electric Boat's submarine cost recording and financial reporting. Nearly half of total backlog—$108.5 billion, including $99.6 billion in Marine Systems—remains unfunded while federal appropriations hang on a Continuing Resolution expiring December 11, 2026.

At the same time, Marine Systems' 7.9 percent margin relied partly on a Virginia Block IV completion adjustment across a 42.9 percent fixed-price nine-month mix. Consolidated nine-month profits included $137 million of favorable EAC catch-ups, net unbilled receivables reached $8,906 million with a $1.2 billion tracked-vehicle variable-consideration warning, Combat Systems lost the M10 Booker program, and $14.52 billion of Technologies goodwill has not had a quantitative test since Q4 2022.

Governance transitions add another layer of execution risk. CEO Phebe Novakovic steps into the Executive Chairman seat on January 1, 2027 as Danny Deep takes over, and she sold 45,353 net shares on Form 4 in November alongside a 12,994-share sale by the General Counsel and a sudden October leadership change at GDIT.

When we price those risks transparently in our probability-weighted 12-month matrix—assigning 50 percent odds to our $355.00 Base Case, 20 percent to a $425.00 Bull Case, and 30 percent to our stressed $245.00 Bear Case—expected value comes to $336.00. Against the $341.50 close, that is minus 1.61 percent expected return. Even at the $339.20 support band top against our $315.00 structural floor, Base Case reward-to-risk is 0.65-to-1, well short of our 1.50-to-1 hurdle.

Notice why we do not hide behind a comfortable WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT hedge. Under our anti-hedging underwriting rules, you may only tell an investor to wait for support when that support zone still delivers at least 1.50-to-1 asymmetry and when the trend is not trapped in a broken Stage 4 decline. Because GD fails both the asymmetry gate and the Stage 4 trend gate while carrying active Note J subpoenas, honesty demands an explicit REJECTED rating.

Across all three time horizons, the answer aligns. Over the short term of one to eight weeks, Stage 4 trend damage, 4-hour RSI at 26.55 without a turn, 10 S&P 500 distribution days, and NO_OPTIONS_EDGE dictate standing aside. Over the medium term of three to twelve months, 0.65-to-1 support asymmetry forces REJECTED at TIER_0. Over the long term, GD belongs strictly on a watch-and-verify list until submarines and governance clear.

Now connect this decision directly to your live portfolio ledger. General Dynamics is NOT_HELD across both Charles Schwab and Robinhood, with zero common shares and zero open option contracts. Nothing needs to be sold. More importantly, your consolidated US portfolio currently holds $75,110.60 in net worth with only $2,540.35 in cash—a 3.38 percent liquidity cushion against the 22.0 percent cash floor required during a market Downtrend.

That cash deficit drives our 100 percent Cash / T-Bills redeployment rule. We benchmark any future marginal dollar against active shortlist leader McKesson—trading in Stage 2 at $1,069.72 with a $1,200.00 Base target, offering 0.64-to-1 asymmetry from its $1,066.70 snapshot band top against an $857.69 stop and requiring a pullback into its $940.00 to $985.00 shortlist entry zone for 1.69-to-1 reward-to-risk—and outside Stage 2 defense peer Lockheed Martin at $565.50 with 16.98 times forward earnings, 21.31 percent ROIC, and 2.64-to-1 asymmetry to $645.00. Both are cleaner than GD today, yet we allocate 0 percent to either until portfolio cash rebuilds toward 22 percent.

For GD itself, four clear signposts would trigger a fresh review: clean closure of the Note J Electric Boat subpoenas in upcoming 2027 filings, passage of full FY2027 defense appropriations beyond December 11, collection of the $1.2 billion unbilled vehicle balance alongside ex-EAC Marine margins above 8.2 percent, and either a deep-value reset into $295 to $310 or a confirmed Stage 2 reclaim above $358.35 on heavy volume.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Downgrading a familiar blue-chip compounder from WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT to REJECTED is uncomfortable—and that is precisely why two-pass unbiased underwriting exists. When federal subpoenas, 0.65:1 support asymmetry, and a confirmed Stage 4 tape align against a 3.38% portfolio cash cushion, walking away is the highest-conviction trade on the board.
